newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Telet cellphone bid valid for now -- Brazil court.
newsitem.headline: Telet cellphone bid valid for now -- Brazil court.

text.p: A Brazilian high court has ruled Telet SA's sealed bid for a prized cellular license will remain valid until it rules definitely on whether the group was legally disqualified last month, an official said.
"The court will probably make a final decision on August 27 or September 10," said a spokesman for the Superior Justice Tribunal (STJ).

The court late Wednesday ruled the government must hold onto Telet's bid for the coveted B Band cellphone area covering non-metropolitan Sao Paulo state pending the outcome of its disqualification appeal, he said.

The decision was latest twist in an ongoing fight by Telet, which includes BCE's Bell Canada and Telesystem International Wireless Inc, to keep alive its hopes of operating one of Brazil's larger B Band concessions.

In late July, Telet appealed Communications Minister Sergio Motta's decision to disqualify it from bidding on larger B Band licenses on ground it was not technically qualified to operate a big concession.
The group won an injunction requiring the ministry to keep its bid on hand in the coveted No. 2 cellphone area covering Sao Paulo state.

The Tess consortium won the No. 2 cellphone area with a winning bid of 1.326 billion reais ($1.2 billion) on Friday, beating out offers by four other groups while Telet's proposal was kept on record but unopened.

However, the Tess victory has effectively been frozen by the group's own legal problems. Tess was also disqualified from the auction, but won an injunction to proceed pending final resolution of its status.
The Tess group includes the Swedish Telia company.
Whatever the outcome of its appeal, Telet, which also includes Malaysia's TRI and Brazilian pension funds, remains in the running for three smaller B Band concessions.
